subject: MedCell expansion — anchor credit, staggered discount & procurement timing
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medcell.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: MedCell expansion — anchor credit, staggered discount & procurement timing

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation and strong alignment on using Redwood for your inference-heavy workflows. As discussed, I put together a short expansion offer that balances your procurement constraints with the economics MedCell needs to scale the new imaging pipeline. See the attached proposal (Redwood_MedCell_Expansion_Proposal_v3.pdf) and the editable order form.

High-level summary of the recommended path:
- Expansion ask: increase reserved capacity by 150k tokens/month equivalent (adds ~2 dedicated GPUs peak).
- Pricing anchor credit: one-time $75,000 credit applied to your next invoice to cover onboarding and early-run costs.
- Staggered uplift discount: 18% discount on the incremental committed units for the first 6 months, then 10% thereafter (if you want a longer promotional period we can bluntly trade off the anchor credit).
- Co-term & billing: We can co-term the uplift to your existing contract end (Dec 31, 2026) or run a 12mo amendment. If procurement needs a single PO + net-45 invoice timing, we can split the uplift into two invoices to match your budget windows.

What I need from you to get legal/procurement moving:
1) Confirmation that procurement is happy with net-45 and PO flow or if they require net-60.
2) Whether you prefer a co-term (aligns to Dec 31) or an independent 12mo amendment.
3) An approximate target date for signature (we've penciled June 10 to preserve the promotional pricing).

If procurement wants to see usage-level justification for the discount I can include our per-token unit economics and an escalation note from our VP of Sales.

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct I’ll route to legal for an amendment and share a DocuSign link. Please review the attached proposal and order form — I left the technical contact as Monica for onboarding coordination.

Best,
David

--
David Kim
Account Executive, Platforms
Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0198

From: Claire Huang <claire@medcell.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medcell.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedCell expansion — anchor credit, staggered discount & procurement timing

Thanks David — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. A few clarifications from procurement and finance: 

- Procurement prefers a single PO and net-45, but must have the order form match the PO lines exactly. They will not accept split invoices without explicit approval from finance.
- Finance is wary of multi-tier discounts tied to later months (they prefer a clean, time-limited promotional discount). Can you do a single-tier promotional discount for the first 12 months instead of 18% then 10%?
- Legal asked to see a clear definition of what counts as "incremental committed units" — they need the exact metric for renewal calculations.

Also, our Director of ML Ops is pushing a bit on the ramp profile: initial usage may be 30% of the committed capacity in month 1, ramping to full in ~3 months. That matters for us from a cash-flow perspective.

I’ll loop procurement on this thread — they may have a few contract language requests. If you can send a redline-friendly order form and a short plain-English amendment summary for legal, that will speed us up.

Thanks,
Claire

—
Claire Huang
Head of Platform Engineering
MedCell

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: MedCell negotiation playbook

David / Monica — quick internal note with a recommended counter that keeps the economics attractive while addressing MedCell's procurement asks.

Proposal (internal, for approval):
- Keep the $75k anchor credit (applies to first invoice post-amendment).
- Offer a single promotional discount of 15% on incremental committed units for 12 months (clean, easier for finance).
- Define "incremental committed units" as: additional reserved token capacity above their current baseline as of signing date, measured in reserved token-months. Add an explicit example in the amendment (we’ll include a table).
- Invoice flow: one PO, one invoice at amendment effective date. If Finance insists on cost smoothing, offer a paid-split option (MedCell pays 50% up front, 50% on net-45) — but only if they accept full anchor credit application.
- Co-term: encourage co-term to Dec 31, 2026 (we waive any early-exit penalties for the uplift portion if they decide to downscale within 90 days).

Why this should work: 15% for 12mo is close to their ask and simpler operationally; anchor credit preserves headline concession while protecting ARR. The paid-split variant gives flexibility without us giving an additional discount.

Action items:
- David: send revised one-page amendment summary + redline-friendly order form tomorrow morning.
- Monica: prepare a short example table that shows 3-month ramp and how credits apply (put in the order form).

If we want to preserve margin further, we can require signature by June 10 to lock the 15% promoter.

- Ben

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@medcell.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedCell expansion — anchor credit, staggered discount & procurement timing

Claire — thanks, and great context. Per internal alignment we’ve simplified the offer to make finance and legal reviews faster. Attached are: 1) a one-page amendment summary, 2) a redline-friendly order form (MedCell_Order_Form_v2.xlsx), and 3) the updated proposal PDF.

Final offer (valid until June 10):
- Anchor credit: $75,000 one-time credit applied to the first invoice after amendment effective date.
- Promotional pricing: 15% off incremental committed units for 12 months (clear single-tier discount as requested).
- Definition: "Incremental committed units" = reserved token capacity above MedCell's baseline as of the amendment signature date; example table included in the order form.
- Billing & PO: We will accept a single PO and issue a single invoice at amendment effective date with net-45. If finance requires smoothing, we can offer a paid-split (50% upfront, 50% net-45) while preserving the anchor credit.
- Co-term: Option to co-term to Dec 31, 2026 at MedCell's election. If MedCell downscales within 90 days of amendment, we will waive early-exit charges for the uplift portion.

Next steps:
1) Review attached files and share any specific redlines (legal likes tracked changes).
2) If procurement is good with PO + net-45, confirm PO number and desired effective date.
3) If all is good I will send a DocuSign link and route to finance/legal.

If it helps, we can also run a short 2-week ramp assurance plan with Monica's team to optimize early usage and reduce initial overprovisioning risk.

Look forward to your thoughts — happy to hop on a 20 minute call with procurement/legal to close this quickly.

Best,
David

--
David Kim
Account Executive, Platforms
Redwood Inference
